newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall despite banking gains.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall despite banking gains.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell 0.15 percent in quiet trade on Monday despite banking sector gains.
Cairo Amman Bank, which aims to more than double its capital to 25 million dinars, rose 0.10 dinars to 5.60 dinars in the trade worth over 80,000 dinars.
The bank, Monday's busiest stock on the Amman bourse, has consistently been in demand from local investors, broker Ibrahim Odeh said.
Jordan Gulf Bank and Jordan National Bank also rose 0.01 dinars to 0.88 and 2.06 dinars respectively in more subdued trade, but Housing Bank slipped back 0.02 dinars to 4.93 dinars.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.15 percent to 159.25 points in turnover of 427,000 dinars.
"The turnover was weak and there's no buying demand," Odeh said, adding that Monday's business was mainly from local investors.
Jordan Kuwait Bank, which delayed an extraordinary general meeting planned for next week by three weeks, rose 0.05 dinars to 3.21 dinars in trade worth 18,000 dinars.
Brokers say a tussle for boardroom control of the bank, linked to a possible takeover by Bank of Jordan, has stimulated trading this week.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers on Monday by 16 to 12, with another 12 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.25 percent to 81.59 points, 2.16 percent down from the start of the year.
